source_text: IV. Quodam autem tempore media nocte, residente pro tribunali praeside Probo, introductus est iterum beatissimus martyr Irenaeus. Probus dixit ad eum: Iam sacrifica, Irenaee, lucrans poenas. Irenaeus respondit: Fac quod iussum est, hoc a me non exspectes. Probus indignatus eum fustibus caedi praecepit. Irenaeus respondit: Deum habeo, quem a prima aetate colere didici: ipsum adoro, qui me confortat in omnibus, cui etiam et sacrifico; deos vero manu factos adorare non possum. Probus dixit: Lucrare mortem. iam tibi sufficiant quae tolerasti tormenta. Irenaeus respondit: Lucror continuo mortem quando per eas quas mihi putas inferre poenas, quas ego non sentio, propter deum accipio vitam aeternam. Probus dixit: Uxorem habes? Irenaeus respondit: Non habeo. Probus dixit: Filios habes? Irenaeus respondit: Non habeo. Probus dixit: Parentes habes? Irenaeus respondit: Non habeo. Probus dixit: Et qui fuerunt illi qui praeterita flebant sessione? Irenaeus respondit: Praeceptum est domini mei Iesu Christi dicentis: Qui diligit patrem aut matrem aut uxorem aut filios aut fratres aut parentes super me, non est me dignus. itaque ad deum in caelum adspiciens et ad eius promissiones intendens, omnia despiciens nullum parentem absque eo se nosse atque habere fatebatur. Probus dixit: Vel propter illos sacrifica. Irenaeus respondit: Filii mei deum habent quem et ego, qui potest illos salvare. tu autem fac quod tibi praeceptum est. Probus dixit: Consule tibi, iuvenis. immola, ut non te cruciatibus impendam. Irenaeus respondit: Fac quod vis. iam nunc videbis quantam mihi dominus Iesus Christus dabit tolerantiam adversus tuas insidias. Probus dixit: Dabo in te sententiam. Irenaeus respondit: Gratulor si feceris. Probus data sententia dixit: Irenaeum inobedientem praeceptis regalibus in fluvium praecipitari iubeo. Irenaeus respondit: Multifarias minas tuas et tormenta plurima exspectabam, ut etiam post haec me ferro subiiceres. tu autem nihil horum intulisti. unde hoc facias oro, ut cognoscas quemadmodum Christiani propter fidem, quae est in deo, mortem contemnere consueverunt.
pass_a_gloss: Literal sense: At midnight Probus sits at the tribunal and Irenaeus is brought in again. Probus orders sacrifice in order to gain escape from punishments. Irenaeus refuses and tells him to do what was commanded. Probus in anger orders beating with clubs. Irenaeus says he has God worshipped from earliest youth, adored and sacrificed to, strengthening him in all things, and he cannot adore handmade gods. Probus urges gaining death and says the tortures endured should suffice. Irenaeus says he gains death continually when through supposed pains, which he does not feel, he receives eternal life on account of God. Probus asks about wife, sons, parents; Irenaeus says he has none. Probus asks who wept at the former hearing. Irenaeus cites his Lord Jesus Christ commanding that one loving father or mother or wife or children or brothers or kinsmen above him is not worthy of him, and says that looking to God in heaven and intent on his promises and despising all things he confessed he knew and had no kinsman except him. Probus says sacrifice at least for their sake. Irenaeus says his sons have the God whom he also has, who can save them, and tells Probus to do what was commanded to him. Probus advises self-care as a young man and sacrifice to avoid tortures. Irenaeus says do what you will, and Probus will now see what endurance the Lord Jesus Christ will give against his plots. Probus says he will give sentence; Irenaeus rejoices if he does. With sentence given Probus orders disobedient Irenaeus to regal commands to be thrown into the river. Irenaeus says he expected manifold threats and many tortures, even subjection to the sword after these, but Probus inflicted none of them, and he begs him to do this, that he may know how Christians through faith in God are accustomed to despise death.
pass_b_english: At one time, in the middle of the night, while the governor Probus sat before the tribunal, the most blessed martyr Irenaeus was brought in again.

Probus said to him, “Now sacrifice, Irenaeus, and buy off your punishments.” Irenaeus answered, “Do what has been commanded; do not expect this from me.” Enraged, Probus ordered him to be beaten with clubs.

Irenaeus answered, “I have God, whom I learned to worship from my earliest youth: him I adore, who strengthens me in all things, and to him I also offer sacrifice; but gods made by hands I cannot adore.” Probus said, “Win death as your gain.

Let the tortures you have endured now be enough for you.” Irenaeus answered, “I win death as continual gain whenever, through these punishments which you think you inflict and which I do not feel, I receive eternal life for God’s sake.” Probus said, “Do you have a wife?” Irenaeus answered, “I do not.” Probus said, “Do you have children?” Irenaeus answered, “I do not.” Probus said, “Do you have parents?” Irenaeus answered, “I do not.” Probus said, “Then who were those who wept at the former hearing?” Irenaeus answered, “It is the command of my Lord Jesus Christ, who says, ‘Whoever loves father or mother or wife or children or brothers or kinsmen more than me is not worthy of me’ (Matthew 10:37); and so, gazing toward God in heaven and fixing his mind on his promises and despising all else, he declared that he knew and had no kinsman apart from him.” Probus said, “At least for their sake, sacrifice.” Irenaeus answered, “My children have God, whom I also have, who is able to save them; but you, do what has been commanded you.” Probus said, “Spare yourself, young man.
Offer sacrifice, lest I hand you over to torments.” Irenaeus answered, “Do what you will.

Even now you shall see what endurance the Lord Jesus Christ will grant me against your plots.” Probus said, “I shall pass sentence upon you.” Irenaeus answered, “I rejoice if you do so.” After passing sentence, Probus said, “I order Irenaeus, disobedient to the royal commands, to be cast headlong into the river.” Irenaeus answered, “I expected your manifold threats and many tortures, and even that after these you would subject me to the sword.
But you have inflicted none of these things.
Therefore I beg you to do this, that you may learn how Christians, through the faith that is in God, are accustomed to scorn death.”

choices.term: lucrans poenas / Lucrare mortem / Lucror continuo mortem
choices.english: buy off punishments / win death as gain / I win death as continual gain
choices.why: lucrari here is ironic commercial language in the interrogation: Probus treats sacrifice as profit escaping penalty, while Irenaeus inverts it so that dying yields eternal life
dative tibi with imperative consule is advisory self-interest, not legal consultation, given the following purpose clause to sacrifice to avoid tortures

choices.term: nullum parentem absque eo se nosse
choices.english: he knew no kinsman apart from him
choices.why: parens here continues the list of wife, children, father, mother, brothers, so it means kin generally rather than father strictly
rejected: he knew no father without him
